title: Change feeds for Reference, ReviewRequest, Message, LocalizationRequest and Delivery
description:
The Item change feed (PPY-8a374e) turns Item changes into wakes. Do the same for the other tables agents react to, one small function per table with a filter in the event source mapping: a Reference created, accepted, rated or re-captured; a review request answered; a Message posted by a person on a subject; a LocalizationRequest wanted; a Delivery state change. Each feed emits the same normalized change (`table, kind, id, lineage, version, change, actorKind, at`) and looks up which agents listen in the site's cached agent definitions (read by the tenant index, never a table list). A table already at two stream readers gets its feed by moving an existing reader behind the feed, not by adding a third.

**Acceptance criteria**
- Each listed change produces a wake for every agent whose definition listens for it, and for no other.
- No feed reads a whole table.
- No table has more than two stream readers.
- Every behaviour change ships with narrative Gherkin specs (below).

**Gherkin features needed**
- change-feeds.feature: accepting a Reference wakes the agents that listen for it; answering a review request wakes the agent that asked; a person's Message on a Story wakes the Story's agents; an agent's own write does not wake itself for the same version; a change nobody listens for sends nothing.

**Infrastructure as code touched:** Site backend: stream enabled on ReviewRequest and Delivery tables; event source mappings with filters; one feed function. Staged where a table gains a stream.

**Part of:** Inbox: change feeds, the wake queue and one worker. Slice code B3 in `docs/design/always-on-agents-architecture.md` (section 12).
**Standing rules:** no fallbacks, no workarounds, no interim systems, no arbitrary caps; no text in DynamoDB; indexes over scans; no AppSync subscriptions; nothing created by hand in AWS; no real email addresses in specs or fixtures; status shown as words and marks, never colour alone.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Built on feat/PPY-9b9e64-change-feeds (fakes and local specs; nothing deployed). Decisions: (1) ONE feed function for the five tables, papyrus-<site>-change-feed, not one per table: the code is shared, the stream ARN in each record names the table, and one function costs function+role+policy (3) plus one mapping per stream it reads itself (8 resources for a site with every table; first stage 1,978 before and after). The design's B3 purpose text says one function per table, its infrastructure line says one feed function; the infrastructure line was followed. (2) Reader placement is a rule in amplify/agents/stream-readers.ts: fewer than two readers means a mapping of its own; two or more means the feed sits behind a reader that stays on the stream and relays its batch (Reference: word index; Message: Slack delivery, else the home page thread reader). test:agents-stack places every combination of the six readers and asserts no table is given a third reader. (3) Message stream already has THREE readers when console responder, Slack and home page are all on: the feed adds none, but that site stays over the guidance until an existing reader moves; not done here. (4) A comment's subject comes from its thread anchor via one getMessageThread point read, made only when some agent listens for a posted Message. (5) change vocabulary (src/papyrus_content/change_vocabulary.py) is now enforced in agent definitions; the earlier test fixtures used Item/ready, which no feed produces, and were changed to step_changed. Remaining live proof (needs a deploy, not done): on a real site, accept a Reference / answer a review request / comment on a Story / move a Delivery state and see one wake per listening agent on the queue, a repeat sends none, the dead-letter queue stays empty; confirm ReviewRequest and Delivery streams appear and the relay from the word index and Slack delivery reaches the function. Leftovers: the third Message reader; Delivery actor comes from the last history line (an agent writer must use the automation: prefix); retained empty poetry venv papyrus-newsroom-kr3-iH9A-py3.12 left behind by a poetry run in a new worktree.
